Network

Zone transfer test protocol

The architecture handoff chapter specifies authority; this page specifies repeatable implementation tests.

On this page
Configure fixtureAssertionsMechanism

Configure fixture

  1. Create two independent processes: Zone_A loads L_Rillmere, Zone_B loads L_Thornweald; same protocol/catalog, separate ZoneProcessIds.
  2. Assign DA_Zone_Rillmere north gate to gate.thornweald.south and the reverse gate back to gate.rillmere.north. Register safe spawns and capacity.
  3. Create Account_A/B and durable Character_A/B. Give A a known sword GUID, ore count, wallet, quest revision and current epoch using backend test fixtures, not a shipping UI cheat.
  4. Connect both to A, record B position/zone, and use A gate. Observe loading, target admission, appearance and same durable facts.
  5. Attempt to use old ticket twice and send a late source epoch write. Both must fail without another pawn/reward.
  6. Repeat with full target, source crash before redemption, target crash after redemption, client lost during loading and unknown catalog; compare failure matrix.

Assertions

Only A changes zone. B stays connected and can continue combat. Source cannot commit after target redemption. Destination creates exactly one body and initializes new PlayerState ASC when relevant. Quest/item/coin state survives without grant replay; source UI delegates are not left bound to destroyed objects.

Mechanism

Use the validated individual PlayerController ClientTravel route. Do not call ServerTravel for this gate test. Internal streaming is a separate map-memory optimization and supplies none of the ticket/epoch guarantees.

Evidence and external references

External links need internet; the manual itself remains offline. Public documentation does not prove installed compatibility.

  • Travelling in multiplayer — Public 5.8 documentation checked; distinguish individual ClientTravel, whole-world ServerTravel and level streaming.
